records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם וּנְתָ֨נְךָ֜ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עֶלְי֔וֹן עַ֖ל כָּל־גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, if listening you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, to keep to do all his commandments which I [am] commanding you today, and will set you Yahweh your God high above all [the] nations of the earth.
pieces: If you truly obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and carefully keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I am giving you today, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will raise you high above every nation on earth.

L.1: And it will be, if you carefully listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, taking care to do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I am commanding you today, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.

R.1: Obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God completely, and be careful to do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands that I am giving you today. If you do, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make you greater than all the nations on earth.

decisions.choice: listening you listen: listen closely, obey fully
decisions.reason: The verb "listen" is doubled, which makes it emphatic: really listen. To "listen to the voice" of the LORD means to obey him, as the next words show: "taking care to do all his commandments" (15:5; 13:19).

decisions.choice: And it will be, if: the condition on which the blessings depend
decisions.reason: The chapter sets out two ways. If Israel obeys, the blessings of verses 1-14 follow; if it does not, the curses of verses 15-68 follow. It goes on from the ceremony of blessing and curse that Moses has just ordered for Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal (27:12-26; 11:26-29).

decisions.choice: high: raised in honor above the other nations
decisions.reason: The word means "highest, uppermost". The LORD has already promised to set Israel high above all nations "in praise, in name and in honor" (26:19); verse 13 says the same with the picture of head and tail.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: Moses' words opened at 27:12 and run on to the end of 28:68, where the double quotation mark closes; this record has none.

decisions.choice: truly obey (Balanced); Obey ... completely (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "listen to the voice". Balanced and Readable say "obey", which is what the phrase means, and carry the doubled verb with "truly" and "completely".

decisions.choice: Obey ... If you do,
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long condition into two plain commands and then gives the promise in a sentence of its own.

records.heading: Blessings for obeying

records.source: וּבָ֧אוּ עָלֶ֛יךָ כָּל־הַבְּרָכ֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְהִשִּׂיגֻ֑ךָ כִּ֣י תִשְׁמַ֔ע בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will come on you all the blessings these and overtake you, if you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God.
pieces: All these blessings will come on you and catch up with you, if you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.2: And all these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.2: If you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, all these blessings will come to you. They will follow you and find you.

decisions.choice: overtake: catch up with, reach
decisions.reason: The verb is used of someone who pursues and catches up with another (19:6; Exodus 14:9). The blessings are pictured as running after Israel until they reach it. The same words are used of the curses in verses 15 and 45.

decisions.choice: catch up with you (Balanced); follow you and find you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of pursuit in plain words; Literal says "overtake". The same wording is used for the curses in verses 15 and 45.

records.source: בָּר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בָּעִ֑יר וּבָר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Blessed [are] you in the city, and blessed [are] you in the field.
pieces: You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the countryside.

L.3: Blessed [are] you in the city, and blessed [are] you in the field.

R.3: You will be blessed in town and in the country.

decisions.choice: Blessed are you: a declaration of what will be
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb, only "blessed you". In this setting, after verse 2, it declares what will come to pass if Israel obeys. The six lines of verses 3-6 are matched by six curses in verses 16-19.

decisions.choice: in the city and in the field: everywhere you live and work
decisions.reason: The pair covers the whole of life: the walled town where people lived and the open country where they farmed and kept flocks.

decisions.choice: You will be blessed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the statement a future, as the promise of verse 2 implies. Literal keeps "Blessed [are] you", bracketing the verb. Verse 16 uses the same wording with "cursed".

records.source: בָּר֧וּךְ פְּרִֽי־בִטְנְךָ֛ וּפְרִ֥י אַדְמָתְךָ֖ וּפְרִ֣י בְהֶמְתֶּ֑ךָ שְׁגַ֥ר אֲלָפֶ֖יךָ וְעַשְׁתְּר֥וֹת צֹאנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Blessed [is the] fruit of your womb and [the] fruit of your ground and [the] fruit of your livestock, [the] young of your cattle and [the] young of your flock.
pieces: Blessed will be the children you bear, the harvest of your soil and the young of your livestock, the young of your cattle and your sheep.

L.4: Blessed [is] the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.

R.4: Your children will be blessed, and your crops, and the young of your animals, the calves in your herds and the lambs in your flocks.

decisions.choice: fruit of your womb, of your ground, of your livestock: children, crops and young animals
decisions.reason: "Fruit" is what comes from something: children from the womb, harvests from the ground, young from the animals. The list repeats the promise of 7:13 and comes back in verses 11, 18 and 51.

decisions.choice: offspring of your cattle, young of your flock
decisions.reason: These are ordinary words for the young born to cattle and to sheep and goats, as in 7:13. They spell out what "the fruit of your livestock" means.

decisions.choice: children you bear, harvest of your soil, young of your livestock; calves, lambs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the pictures mean, as at 7:13; Literal keeps "fruit". The same wording is used in verse 18.

records.source: בָּר֥וּךְ טַנְאֲךָ֖ וּמִשְׁאַרְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Blessed [is] your basket and your kneading bowl.
pieces: Blessed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.

L.5: Blessed [is] your basket and your kneading bowl.

R.5: The basket you gather your harvest in and the bowl you make bread in will be blessed.

decisions.choice: basket and kneading bowl: the harvest and the daily bread made from it
decisions.reason: The basket held produce gathered from the fields, as in the offering of first fruits (26:2, 4). The kneading bowl was where dough was mixed and kneaded for bread (Exodus 12:34). Together they stand for food from the harvest to the table.

decisions.choice: you gather your harvest in; you make bread in
decisions.reason: Readable says what each container was used for, so the reader sees that the blessing is on food. Verse 17 uses the same wording with "cursed".

records.source: בָּר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בְּבֹאֶ֑ךָ וּבָר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בְּצֵאתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Blessed [are] you in your coming in, and blessed [are] you in your going out.
pieces: You will be blessed as you come in and blessed as you go out.

L.6: Blessed [are] you in your coming in, and blessed [are] you in your going out.

R.6: You will be blessed when you come in and when you go out, in everything you do.

decisions.choice: coming in and going out: all of your daily activity
decisions.reason: The pair covers every movement of life, going out to work or to war and coming home again (31:2; Psalm 121:8).

decisions.choice: in everything you do
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the pair means. Verse 19 uses the same wording with "cursed".

records.source: יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־אֹיְבֶ֨יךָ֙ הַקָּמִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ נִגָּפִ֖ים לְפָנֶ֑יךָ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אֶחָד֙ יֵצְא֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וּבְשִׁבְעָ֥ה דְרָכִ֖ים יָנ֥וּסוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Will make Yahweh your enemies who rise against you defeated before you; by way one they will come out against you, and by seven ways they will flee before you.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will let you defeat the enemies who rise up against you. They will march out against you by one road and flee from you by seven.

L.7: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make your enemies who rise up against you defeated before you; by one way they will come out against you, and by seven ways they will flee before you.

R.7: When enemies attack you, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will let you defeat them. They will come at you from one direction, but they will run away from you in seven directions.

decisions.choice: by one way ... by seven ways: they come as one army and scatter in every direction
decisions.reason: The enemy marches out in good order along one road and runs away in panic along many. Seven is a number of fullness: they scatter every way they can. Verse 25 turns the same picture against Israel.

decisions.choice: will make ... defeated before you: the LORD gives the victory
decisions.reason: The LORD is the subject: he is the one who strikes the enemy down, though Israel fights the battle (20:4).

decisions.choice: will let you defeat
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "make ... defeated before you". Balanced and Readable make Israel the one who defeats, with the LORD as the one who lets it happen.

records.source: יְצַ֨ו יְהוָ֤ה אִתְּךָ֙ אֶת־הַבְּרָכָ֔ה בַּאֲסָמֶ֕יךָ וּבְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֣ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וּבֵ֣רַכְךָ֔ בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Will command Yahweh with you the blessing in your barns and in all [the] undertaking of your hand, and he will bless you in the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will command blessing to be with you in your barns and in everything you set your hand to. He will bless you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

L.8: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in all the undertaking of your hand, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless you in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you.

R.8: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give the order, and blessing will fill your barns and rest on all your work. He will bless you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

decisions.choice: command the blessing: order blessing to come by his word
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks and the blessing comes, as a king's command is carried out (Leviticus 25:21; Psalm 133:3).

decisions.choice: the undertaking of your hand: whatever you work at
decisions.reason: The phrase means everything a person sets to work on and what it produces (12:7; 15:10).

decisions.choice: blessing will fill your barns
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blessing in the barns means: stores of grain. Literal and Balanced keep "the blessing ... in your barns".

records.source: יְקִֽימְךָ֨יְהוָ֥ה לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם קָד֔וֹשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע־לָ֑ךְ כִּ֣י תִשְׁמֹ֗ר אֶת־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֖ בִּדְרָכָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Will establish you Yahweh for himself as a people holy, just as he swore to you, if you keep [the] commandments of Yahweh your God and walk in his ways.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you a people holy to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you on oath, as long as you keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways.

L.9: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will establish you for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as a holy people, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to you, if you keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways.

R.9: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own holy people, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you with an oath. But you must obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants you to live.

decisions.choice: a holy people for himself: set apart as his own
decisions.reason: Israel is holy because the LORD has chosen it and set it apart to belong to him (7:6; 14:2; 26:19; Exodus 19:5-6).

decisions.choice: establish: raise up and make firm
decisions.reason: The verb means to set up and confirm, so that what is promised stands and lasts. The LORD will make Israel firmly what he has sworn it will be.

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as he directs
decisions.reason: Walking stands for the whole way a person lives (8:6; 10:12; 11:22).

decisions.choice: live the way he wants you to live
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "walk in his ways"; Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

records.source: וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה נִקְרָ֣א עָלֶ֑יךָ וְיָֽרְא֖וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: And will see all [the] peoples of the earth that [the] name of Yahweh is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.
pieces: Then every people on earth will see that you bear the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will be afraid of you.

L.10: And all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.

R.10: Then all the nations on earth will see that you belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will be afraid of you.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD is called over you: you belong to him
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over a thing or a people means that it belongs to him (2 Samuel 12:28; Jeremiah 14:9). The nations will see that Israel is the LORD's own people.

decisions.choice: afraid of you: in awe of the people the LORD protects
decisions.reason: The nations fear Israel because of the God who stands behind it, as promised in 2:25 and 11:25.

decisions.choice: bear the name (Balanced); belong to (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced makes Israel the subject; Readable says what the idiom means. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

records.source: וְהוֹתִֽרְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ לְטוֹבָ֔ה בִּפְרִ֧י בִטְנְךָ֛ וּבִפְרִ֥י בְהַמְתְּךָ֖ וּבִפְרִ֣י אַדְמָתֶ֑ךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה לַאֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ לָ֥תֶת לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And will make you abound Yahweh in good, in [the] fruit of your womb and in [the] fruit of your livestock and in [the] fruit of your ground, on the ground which swore Yahweh to your fathers to give to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you plenty of good things: many children, many young among your livestock and rich harvests from your soil, in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your ancestors to give you.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you abound in good things, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, on the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers to give to you.

R.11: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you more than enough of everything good. You will have many children, many young animals and big harvests. All this will be in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised your ancestors with an oath to give you.

decisions.choice: make you abound in good: give you more than enough
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave over, to give in excess. "Good" here is prosperity, the good things of the land.

decisions.choice: swore to your fathers: the promise of the land to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The land is the one the LORD promised on oath to Israel's ancestors (1:8; Genesis 12:7; 26:3; 28:13).

decisions.choice: many children, many young, rich harvests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the three kinds of "fruit" are, as in verse 4, and carry "abound" into "many" and "rich". Literal keeps "fruit".

records.source: יִפְתַּ֣ח יְהוָ֣ה׀לְ֠ךָ אֶת־אוֹצָר֨וֹ הַטּ֜וֹב אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם לָתֵ֤ת מְטַֽר־אַרְצְךָ֙ בְּעִתּ֔וֹ וּלְבָרֵ֕ךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֑ךָ וְהִלְוִ֨יתָ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א תִלְוֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Will open Yahweh for you his storehouse the good, the heavens, to give [the] rain of your land in its time and to bless all [the] work of your hand; and you will lend to nations many, and you will not borrow.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will open for you the heavens, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rich storehouse, to send rain on your land at the right time and to bless all that your hands do. You will lend to many nations and borrow from none.

L.12: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will open for you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good storehouse, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hand; and you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

R.12: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will open the sky, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good gifts, and send rain on your land at the right time. He will bless all your work. You will lend to many nations, but you will not need to borrow from any.

decisions.choice: his good storehouse, the heavens: the sky as the store of rain
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as a storehouse from which the LORD sends rain (Job 38:22; Jeremiah 10:13). The land of Canaan depended on rain, not on a river as Egypt did (11:10-14).

decisions.choice: in its season: the autumn and spring rains
decisions.reason: The rains had to come at the right times for sowing and for the ripening of the crops (11:14).

decisions.choice: lend to many nations and not borrow: wealth and freedom
decisions.reason: The lender has power and the borrower depends on him (15:6; Proverbs 22:7). Verse 44 turns this around.

decisions.choice: where he keeps his good gifts
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the storehouse. Literal and Balanced keep it.

records.source: וּנְתָֽנְךָ֨ יְהוָ֤ה לְרֹאשׁ֙ וְלֹ֣א לְזָנָ֔ב וְהָיִ֨יתָ֙ רַ֣ק לְמַ֔עְלָה וְלֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לְמָ֑טָּה כִּֽי־תִשְׁמַ֞ע אֶל־מִצְוֺ֣ת׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ הַיּ֖וֹם לִשְׁמֹ֥ר וְלַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And will make you Yahweh [the] head and not [the] tail, and you will be only above and not you will be below, if you listen to [the] commandments of Yahweh your God which I [am] commanding you today to keep and to do,
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you the head, never the tail; you will always be at the top and never at the bottom, if you heed the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you today and carefully keep them,

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you the head and not the tail, and you will be only above and you will not be below, if you listen to the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am commanding you today, to keep and to do [them],

R.13: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you the leader and not the follower. You will always be on top, never at the bottom. But you must listen to the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you today, and be careful to obey them.

decisions.choice: head and not tail: leading, not following
decisions.reason: The head goes first and leads; the tail comes last. The picture is of honor and power among the nations (Isaiah 9:13-14). Verse 44 reverses it.

decisions.choice: if you listen ...: the condition goes on into verse 14
decisions.reason: The sentence does not end here: the condition includes not turning aside to other gods in verse 14.

decisions.choice: the leader and not the follower
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means; Literal and Balanced keep "head" and "tail".

decisions.choice: [them]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object that English needs for "to keep and to do".

records.source: וְלֹ֣א תָס֗וּר מִכָּל־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול לָלֶ֗כֶת אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים לְעָבְדָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: and not you turn aside from any of the words which I [am] commanding you today, right or left, to go after gods other to serve them.
pieces: and if you do not turn from any of the words I am giving you today, either to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and serve them.

L.14: and [if] you do not turn aside from any of the words that I am commanding you today, [to the] right or [to the] left, to go after other gods to serve them.

R.14: Do not turn away from anything I am commanding you today, not even a little. Do not follow other gods and worship them.

decisions.choice: right or left: the smallest departure from the way
decisions.reason: Turning to either side of the road means leaving the path the LORD has set, even a little (5:32; 17:11, 20).

decisions.choice: go after other gods to serve them: follow and worship them
decisions.reason: To "go after" a god is to follow it as a loyal subject; to "serve" it is to worship it (6:14; 8:19; 11:28).

decisions.choice: not even a little; worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains "right or left" and says "worship" for "serve". Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew wording.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־לֹ֤א תִשְׁמַע֙ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו וְחֻקֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם וּבָ֧אוּ עָלֶ֛יךָ כָּל־הַקְּלָל֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְהִשִּׂיגֽוּךָ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, if not you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, to keep to do all his commandments and his statutes which I [am] commanding you today, and will come on you all the curses these and overtake you.
pieces: But if you do not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and carefully keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and statutes that I am giving you today, all these curses will come on you and catch up with you.

L.15: And it will be, if you do not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, taking care to do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that I am commanding you today, that all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.

R.15: But if you do not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you are not careful to do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and laws that I am giving you today, all these curses will come to you. They will follow you and find you.

decisions.choice: if you do not listen: the other way, matching verse 1
decisions.reason: The verse mirrors verses 1-2 word for word, with "not" added and "curses" in place of "blessings". The curses that follow answer the blessings line for line (verses 16-19 match verses 3-6) and then go on far longer.

decisions.choice: overtake: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The curses, like the blessings, are pictured as pursuing Israel until they catch it.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the verse with "and". Balanced and Readable say "But", since the verse turns from blessing to curse; Literal keeps "And".

records.heading: Curses for not obeying

L.18: Cursed [is] the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.

R.18: Your children will be cursed, and your crops, and the calves in your herds and the lambs in your flocks.

decisions.choice: fruit of your womb and of your ground: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: Children and crops, as in verse 4. This line leaves out "the fruit of your livestock" but goes on to name the young of the herds and flocks, so the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: same wording as verse 4
decisions.reason: Each level uses the wording of verse 4, so the curse is heard as the exact reverse of the blessing.

records.source: אָר֥וּר אַתָּ֖ה בְּבֹאֶ֑ךָ וְאָר֥וּר אַתָּ֖ה בְּצֵאתֶֽךָ׃

L.19: Cursed [are] you in your coming in, and cursed [are] you in your going out.

R.19: You will be cursed when you come in and when you go out, in everything you do.

decisions.choice: coming in and going out: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: All of daily life will be under the curse. The wording follows verse 6 at every level.

records.source: יְשַׁלַּ֣ח יְהוָ֣ה׀בְּ֠ךָ אֶת־הַמְּאֵרָ֤ה אֶת־הַמְּהוּמָה֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּגְעֶ֔רֶת בְּכָל־מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה עַ֣ד הִשָּֽׁמֶדְךָ֤ וְעַד־אֲבָדְךָ֙ מַהֵ֔ר מִפְּנֵ֛י רֹ֥עַ מַֽעֲלָלֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲזַבְתָּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Will send Yahweh on you the curse, the confusion and the rebuke in all [the] undertaking of your hand which you do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of [the] evil of your deeds by which you have forsaken me.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send on you curse, panic and frustration in everything you set your hand to, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the evil you have done in forsaking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.20: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send on you the curse, the confusion and the rebuke in all the undertaking of your hand that you do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, in that you have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.20: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send curses, panic and failure on everything you try to do, until you are destroyed. You will soon be gone, because you did evil and turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the curse, the confusion, the rebuke
decisions.reason: The first word is a curse that brings ruin. The second is the panic and disorder the LORD sends on his enemies (7:23; 1 Samuel 5:9). The third is a rebuke that blocks and spoils whatever is attempted, so that nothing succeeds.

decisions.choice: forsaken me: the LORD himself speaks
decisions.reason: Moses is speaking, but the words "you have forsaken me" are the LORD's. In Deuteronomy Moses' voice passes into the LORD's own without notice (7:4; 11:14-15; 17:3).

decisions.choice: the undertaking of your hand: as in verse 8
decisions.reason: The blessing on all their work in verse 8 becomes a curse on it.

decisions.choice: me, the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, so that young readers do not take "me" to be Moses.

records.source: יַדְבֵּ֧ק יְהוָ֛ה בְּךָ֖ אֶת־הַדָּ֑בֶר עַ֚ד כַּלֹּת֣וֹ אֹֽתְךָ֔ מֵעַל֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Will make cling Yahweh to you the pestilence until he has finished you from on the ground where you [are] going there to possess it.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make disease cling to you until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has wiped you out from the land you are entering to take possession of.

L.21: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make the pestilence cling to you until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has consumed you from the land that you are going into to take possession of.

R.21: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send deadly disease that will not leave you, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has wiped you out from the land you are going into to take as your own.

decisions.choice: the pestilence: a deadly epidemic
decisions.reason: The word names a plague that kills many, among people or animals (Exodus 9:3, 15; Leviticus 26:25).

decisions.choice: consumed: finished off, brought to an end
decisions.reason: The verb means to complete or finish, and so to destroy entirely.

decisions.choice: take possession of (Balanced); take as your own (Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrase about the land comes back in verse 63 and is worded the same way there at each level.

records.source: יַכְּכָ֣ה יְ֠הוָה בַּשַּׁחֶ֨פֶת וּבַקַּדַּ֜חַת וּבַדַּלֶּ֗קֶת וּבַֽחַרְחֻר֙ וּבַחֶ֔רֶב וּבַשִּׁדָּפ֖וֹן וּבַיֵּרָק֑וֹן וּרְדָפ֖וּךָ עַ֥ד אָבְדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Will strike you Yahweh with consumption and with fever and with inflammation and with fiery heat and with sword and with blight and with mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with wasting disease, fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and the sword, with blight and mildew. They will hunt you down until you perish.

L.22: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with wasting disease and with fever and with inflammation and with fiery heat and with sword and with blight and with mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.

R.22: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with diseases that make you waste away, with fever and swelling. He will send burning heat and war, and diseases that ruin your crops. These troubles will chase you until you die.

decisions.choice: wasting disease, fever, inflammation, fiery heat
decisions.reason: These are names of diseases, probably a sickness that wastes the body, a burning fever, an inflammation and a feverish heat. Exactly which illnesses they were cannot be known. The first two also appear in Leviticus 26:16.

decisions.choice: sword
decisions.reason: The written consonants can be read with different vowels as "drought", which would fit the heat before it and the crop diseases after it. Some ancient translations read it that way. The Hebrew text as pointed reads "sword", and this translation follows it.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew: diseases of grain
decisions.reason: Blight is the scorching of grain by the hot east wind; mildew is a disease that turns the ears yellow. They are named together in 1 Kings 8:37 and Amos 4:9.

decisions.choice: war; diseases that ruin your crops
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword and explains blight and mildew as crop diseases.

records.source: וְהָי֥וּ שָׁמֶ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹאשְׁךָ֖ נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְהָאָ֥רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־תַּחְתֶּ֖יךָ בַּרְזֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And will be your heavens which [are] over your head bronze, and the earth which [is] under you iron.
pieces: The sky above your head will be bronze, and the ground beneath you iron.

L.23: And your heavens that are over your head will be bronze, and the earth that is under you iron.

R.23: The sky above you will be hard like bronze and give no rain. The ground under you will be as hard as iron.

decisions.choice: bronze sky, iron ground: drought
decisions.reason: A sky like metal gives no rain, and ground like iron cannot be ploughed or grow anything (Leviticus 26:19). It is the reverse of the opened storehouse of verse 12.

decisions.choice: and give no rain
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

records.source: יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מְטַ֥ר אַרְצְךָ֖ אָבָ֣ק וְעָפָ֑ר מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ יֵרֵ֣ד עָלֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד הִשָּׁמְדָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Will make Yahweh [the] rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it will come down on you until you are destroyed.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will turn the rain of your land into powder and dust; it will fall on you from the sky until you are destroyed.

L.24: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it will come down on you until you are destroyed.

R.24: Instead of rain, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send dust and sand down from the sky on your land, until you are destroyed.

decisions.choice: powder and dust instead of rain: dust storms
decisions.reason: In a drought the hot wind from the desert fills the air with fine dust, which falls where rain should have fallen.

decisions.choice: Instead of rain
decisions.reason: Readable puts the contrast first, so the picture is clear.

records.source: יִתֶּנְךָ֨יְהוָ֥ה׀נִגָּף֮ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹיְבֶיךָ֒ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אֶחָד֙ תֵּצֵ֣א אֵלָ֔יו וּבְשִׁבְעָ֥ה דְרָכִ֖ים תָּנ֣וּס לְפָנָ֑יו וְהָיִ֣יתָ לְזַעֲוָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Will make you Yahweh defeated before your enemies; by way one you will go out against him, and by seven ways you will flee before him, and you will become a horror to all [the] kingdoms of the earth.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will let your enemies defeat you. You will march out against them by one road and flee from them by seven. You will become a thing of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

L.25: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you defeated before your enemies; by one way you will go out against them, and by seven ways you will flee before them, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

R.25: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will let your enemies defeat you. You will come at them from one direction, but you will run away from them in seven directions. All the kingdoms on earth will be horrified at what has happened to you.

decisions.choice: one way, seven ways: verse 7 turned around
decisions.reason: The words of verse 7 come back with Israel and its enemies changing places.

decisions.choice: a horror: something that makes people shudder
decisions.reason: The word means a terror or object of dread; others see what has happened to Israel and are shaken (Jeremiah 15:4; 24:9).

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him", the enemy as one body. English says "them" at every level, so the pronoun is not taken for one person.

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֤ה נִבְלָֽתְךָ֙ לְמַאֲכָ֔ל לְכָל־ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֣ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאֵ֖ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And will be your corpse food for every bird of the heavens and for [the] animals of the earth, and there [will be] none frightening [them].
pieces: Your dead bodies will be food for all the birds of the sky and the wild animals, and no one will frighten them away.

L.26: And your corpses will be food for every bird of the sky and for the animals of the earth, and [there will be] no one to frighten [them] away.

R.26: Your dead bodies will be eaten by birds and wild animals, and no one will be there to chase them away.

decisions.choice: food for the birds: left unburied
decisions.reason: To lie unburied, eaten by birds and animals, was the worst disgrace that could come to the dead (1 Samuel 17:44; 2 Samuel 21:10; Jeremiah 7:33).

decisions.choice: your corpse: the dead of the whole people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular, but it speaks of the dead of the nation as a whole.

decisions.choice: corpses, dead bodies
decisions.reason: English uses the plural for the Hebrew collective singular.

records.source: יַכְּכָ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה בִּשְׁחִ֤ין מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וּבַטְּחֹרִ֔ים וּבַגָּרָ֖ב וּבֶחָ֑רֶס אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תוּכַ֖ל לְהֵרָפֵֽא׃
records.gloss: Will strike you Yahweh with [the] boil of Egypt and with tumors and with scabs and with itch, which not you will be able to be healed.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs and itch that cannot be cured.

L.27: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors and with scabs and with itch, from which you will not be able to be healed.

R.27: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with the same sores {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent on Egypt, and with swellings and itching skin diseases that cannot be healed.

decisions.choice: the boils of Egypt: the sixth plague
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the boils that broke out on the Egyptians and their animals (Exodus 9:9-11). What the LORD did to Egypt he will do to Israel (verse 60).

decisions.choice: tumors
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell a word that means swellings, perhaps of the bowel. A note in the margin, followed in reading aloud, gives another word with the same meaning that was felt to be less coarse. The same exchange is made in 1 Samuel 5:6-12. This translation follows the word that is read; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: scabs and itch: skin diseases
decisions.reason: Both words name skin diseases that cause scabs and itching (Leviticus 21:20; 22:22). Which ones exactly is not known.

decisions.choice: the same sores he sent on Egypt; swellings and itching skin diseases
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the boils of Egypt" and uses common words for the diseases.

records.source: יַכְּכָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בְּשִׁגָּע֖וֹן וּבְעִוָּר֑וֹן וּבְתִמְה֖וֹן לֵבָֽב׃
records.gloss: Will strike you Yahweh with madness and with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind.

L.28: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with madness and with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.

R.28: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you go mad and blind, and your mind will be confused.

decisions.choice: bewilderment of heart: confusion of mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought in Hebrew. The phrase describes a panic so great that people cannot think. The same three words come together of horses and riders in battle in Zechariah 12:4.

decisions.choice: blindness: of the eyes and of the mind
decisions.reason: The word may mean loss of sight, but beside madness and confusion, and with verse 29, it also describes people who cannot see what to do.

decisions.choice: mind
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mind" for "heart", since the word here is about thinking.

records.source: וְהָיִ֜יתָ מְמַשֵּׁ֣שׁ בַּֽצָּהֳרַ֗יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יְמַשֵּׁ֤שׁ הָעִוֵּר֙ בָּאֲפֵלָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תַצְלִ֖יחַ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֜יתָ אַ֣ךְ עָשׁ֧וּק וְגָז֛וּל כָּל־הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֵ֥ין מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: And you will be groping at noon just as gropes the blind [man] in darkness, and not you will make prosper your ways; and you will be only oppressed and robbed all the days, and there [will be] none saving.
pieces: At noon you will grope like a blind person groping in the dark, and you will not succeed in anything you do. You will be nothing but oppressed and robbed all the time, and no one will come to save you.

L.29: And you will be groping at noon as {{gender:the blind person|the blind man}} gropes in the darkness, and you will not make your ways prosper; and you will be only oppressed and robbed all the days, and [there will be] no one to save [you].

R.29: Even at midday you will feel your way around like a blind person in the dark. Nothing you do will succeed. People will always be mistreating you and robbing you, and no one will rescue you.

decisions.choice: groping at noon: helpless even in full daylight
decisions.reason: Even when the light is brightest, they will feel their way like the blind. It carries on the blindness of mind in verse 28 (Isaiah 59:10).

decisions.choice: oppressed and robbed: cheated and plundered
decisions.reason: The two words are paired in Leviticus 19:13 for wronging a neighbor by force or fraud. Here others will do it to Israel without end. Verse 33 has a similar line.

decisions.choice: you will not make your ways prosper: nothing you do will succeed
decisions.reason: "Ways" are a person's undertakings, and "make prosper" means bring to success.

decisions.choice: the blind person / the blind man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a masculine form used for any blind person, so Literal gives an inclusive default with the traditional form as the alternative.

records.source: אִשָּׁ֣ה תְאָרֵ֗שׂ וְאִ֤ישׁ אַחֵר֙ יִשְׁכָּבֶ֔נָּה בַּ֥יִת תִּבְנֶ֖ה וְלֹא־תֵשֵׁ֣ב בּ֑וֹ כֶּ֥רֶם תִּטַּ֖ע וְלֹ֥א תְחַלְּלֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: A woman you will betroth, and a man another will lie with her; a house you will build, and not you will dwell in it; a vineyard you will plant, and not you will make common use of it.
pieces: You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but never enjoy its fruit.

L.30: A woman you will betroth, and another man will lie with her; a house you will build, and you will not live in it; a vineyard you will plant, and you will not put it to use.

R.30: You will be engaged to marry a woman, but another man will take her and sleep with her. You will build a house, but you will never live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will never eat its grapes.

decisions.choice: betrothed wife, new house, new vineyard: the things that excused a man from war
decisions.reason: In 20:5-7 a man who had built a new house, planted a vineyard or become engaged was sent home from battle so that he would not die and leave them to another. Here the curse takes all three from him while he lives.

decisions.choice: lie with her
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text give a coarser verb for sex. A note in the margin, followed in reading aloud, gives "lie with her" instead, as also in Isaiah 13:16, Jeremiah 3:2 and Zechariah 14:2. The meaning is the same; the woman is taken by force.

decisions.choice: put it to use: begin to eat its fruit
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common, to bring into ordinary use. The fruit of a new vineyard could not be eaten for its first years (Leviticus 19:23-25); the owner who has waited will never get to enjoy it (20:6).

decisions.choice: enjoy its fruit (Balanced); eat its grapes (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what putting a vineyard to use means; Literal keeps "put it to use".

records.source: שׁוֹרְךָ֞ טָב֣וּחַ לְעֵינֶ֗יךָ וְלֹ֣א תֹאכַל֮ מִמֶּנּוּ֒ חֲמֹֽרְךָ֙ גָּז֣וּל מִלְּפָנֶ֔יךָ וְלֹ֥א יָשׁ֖וּב לָ֑ךְ צֹֽאנְךָ֙ נְתֻנ֣וֹת לְאֹיְבֶ֔יךָ וְאֵ֥ין לְךָ֖ מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: Your ox [will be] slaughtered before your eyes, and not you will eat of it; your donkey [will be] robbed from before you, and not it will return to you; your flock [will be] given to your enemies, and there [will be] none for you saving.
pieces: Your ox will be slaughtered in front of you, but you will eat none of it. Your donkey will be seized from you by force and never returned. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and no one will come to save you.

L.31: Your ox [will be] slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it; your donkey [will be] robbed from before you, and it will not come back to you; your flock [will be] given to your enemies, and [there will be] no one to save you.

R.31: Your ox will be killed while you watch, but you will not get to eat any of it. Your donkey will be stolen right in front of you, and you will never get it back. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will rescue you.

decisions.choice: robbed: seized by force
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for "robbed" in verse 29: taken openly by someone stronger.

decisions.choice: ox, donkey and flock: the wealth of a farming household
decisions.reason: The ox pulled the plough, the donkey carried loads, and the flock gave milk, wool and meat. Losing them meant losing the means to live.

records.source: בָּנֶ֨יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֜יךָ נְתֻנִ֨ים לְעַ֤ם אַחֵר֙ וְעֵינֶ֣יךָ רֹא֔וֹת וְכָל֥וֹת אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְאֵ֥ין לְאֵ֖ל יָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Your sons and your daughters [will be] given to a people another, and your eyes [will be] looking and failing for them all the day, and there [will be] no power of your hand.
pieces: Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people while you look on. Your eyes will wear themselves out longing for them all day long, and you will be powerless to do anything.

L.32: Your sons and your daughters [will be] given to another people, and your eyes [will be] looking and failing for them all the day, and [there will be] no power in your hand.

R.32: Your sons and daughters will be given to foreigners, and you will watch it happen. Every day you will look for them and long for them until your eyes grow tired, but you will be able to do nothing.

decisions.choice: eyes looking and failing: worn out with longing
decisions.reason: The eyes "fail" or wear out from watching for someone who does not come (Psalm 69:4; Lamentations 4:17). Parents will watch their children taken away and look for their return in vain.

decisions.choice: no power in your hand: helpless
decisions.reason: The phrase means there is nothing one can do. It is used of parents whose children are sold into slavery in Nehemiah 5:5 (see also Genesis 31:29; Micah 2:1).

decisions.choice: while you look on (Balanced); you will watch it happen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your eyes looking" before "failing". Balanced and Readable put the watching with the giving away, then the longing in a sentence of its own.

records.source: פְּרִ֤י אַדְמָֽתְךָ֙ וְכָל־יְגִ֣יעֲךָ֔ יֹאכַ֥ל עַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־יָדָ֑עְתָּ וְהָיִ֗יתָ רַ֛ק עָשׁ֥וּק וְרָצ֖וּץ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: [The] fruit of your ground and all your toil will eat a people which not you have known, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
pieces: A people you have never known will eat up the harvest of your soil and everything you have worked for, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed all the time.

L.33: The fruit of your ground and all your toil a people whom you have not known will eat, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all the days.

R.33: Foreigners you have never heard of will eat your crops and everything you worked hard for. People will always be mistreating you and crushing you.

decisions.choice: your toil: what your hard work has produced
decisions.reason: The word means labor and also the gain that labor brings, here the produce and goods of the farm.

decisions.choice: a people you have not known: a foreign, unfamiliar nation
decisions.reason: "Not known" means strange and foreign: a nation from far away, with no ties to Israel (verses 36 and 49).

decisions.choice: A people ... will eat up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts what is eaten first and the eaters last; Literal keeps that order and Balanced and Readable put the subject first. The last line is worded as in verse 29.

records.source: וְהָיִ֖יתָ מְשֻׁגָּ֑ע מִמַּרְאֵ֥ה עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will be driven mad from [the] sight of your eyes which you will see.
pieces: You will be driven mad by what you see with your own eyes.

L.34: And you will be driven mad by the sight of your eyes that you will see.

R.34: What you see will drive you out of your mind.

decisions.choice: driven mad: losing one's mind
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "madness" in verse 28. What they see will be more than the mind can bear.

records.source: יַכְּכָ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֗ע עַל־הַבִּרְכַּ֨יִם֙ וְעַל־הַשֹּׁקַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תוּכַ֖ל לְהֵרָפֵ֑א מִכַּ֥ף רַגְלְךָ֖ וְעַ֥ד קָדְקֳדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Will strike you Yahweh with boils bad on the knees and on the legs which not you will be able to be healed, from [the] sole of your foot to your crown of head.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike your knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be cured, spreading from the soles of your feet up to the crown of your head.

L.35: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you with bad boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you will not be able to be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.

R.35: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will cover your knees and legs with painful sores that cannot be healed. They will spread over your whole body, from your feet to the top of your head.

decisions.choice: bad boils from the sole of the foot to the crown of the head
decisions.reason: The same words describe the sores that struck Job (Job 2:7).

decisions.choice: from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head: the whole body
decisions.reason: The pair names the two ends of the body to mean all of it (Isaiah 1:6; 2 Samuel 14:25).

decisions.choice: spreading (Balanced); They will spread over your whole body (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves straight from knees and legs to the whole body. Balanced and Readable supply a word that joins the two.

records.source: יוֹלֵ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֹֽתְךָ֗ וְאֶֽת־מַלְכְּךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּקִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ אֶל־גּ֕וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדַ֖עְתָּ אַתָּ֣ה וַאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וְעָבַ֥דְתָּ שָּׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עֵ֥ץ וָאָֽבֶן׃
records.gloss: Will lead Yahweh you and your king whom you will set over you to a nation which not you have known, you and your fathers, and you will serve there gods other, wood and stone.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring you and the king you set over yourselves to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone.

L.36: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will lead you and your king whom you set over you to a nation that you have not known, you and your fathers, and there you will serve other gods, wood and stone.

R.36: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will take you and the king you have chosen to rule you to a nation you and your ancestors never knew. There you will worship other gods, idols made of wood and stone.

decisions.choice: your king whom you set over you
decisions.reason: Moses has allowed that Israel may one day set a king over itself (17:14-15). That king too will be led away.

decisions.choice: lead ... to a nation: take into exile
decisions.reason: The LORD will bring them out of their own land to live in a foreign one, as captives.

decisions.choice: other gods, wood and stone: idols
decisions.reason: The gods of the nations are images made by human hands (4:28; 29:16). Those who would not serve the LORD will have to serve such gods.

decisions.choice: gods of wood and stone (Balanced); idols made of wood and stone (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "wood and stone" describes the gods. Readable also says "worship" for "serve". Verse 64 uses the same wording.

records.source: וְהָיִ֣יתָ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה לְמָשָׁ֖ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֑ה בְּכֹל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יְנַהֶגְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And you will become a horror, a proverb and a taunt among all the peoples where will drive you Yahweh there.
pieces: You will become an object of horror, a saying and a joke among all the peoples where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drives you.

L.37: And you will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive you.

R.37: In all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends you, people will be shocked at what has happened to you. They will tell stories about you and make fun of you.

decisions.choice: a horror: a sight that appalls
decisions.reason: The word means desolation and the shock felt by those who see it (Jeremiah 25:9, 18).

decisions.choice: a proverb and a byword: a name used in sayings and in mockery
decisions.reason: People will use Israel's name as an example of disaster in their sayings and jokes (1 Kings 9:7; Jeremiah 24:9).

decisions.choice: shocked; tell stories about you and make fun of you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the three nouns mean in sentences of their own.

records.source: זֶ֥רַע רַ֖ב תּוֹצִ֣יא הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּמְעַ֣ט תֶּאֱסֹ֔ף כִּ֥י יַחְסְלֶ֖נּוּ הָאַרְבֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Seed much you will take out [to] the field, and little you will gather, for will consume it the locust.
pieces: You will take much seed out to the field but gather little, because locusts will devour it.

L.38: Much seed you will carry out to the field, and little you will gather in, for the locust will consume it.

R.38: You will plant a lot of seed in your fields, but you will harvest very little, because locusts will eat it.

decisions.choice: the locust: swarms that strip the fields
decisions.reason: Swarms of locusts could eat every green thing in a region (Exodus 10:12-15; Joel 1:4).

decisions.choice: it: the crop that grows from the seed
decisions.reason: What the locust eats is the growing grain.

records.source: כְּרָמִ֥ים תִּטַּ֖ע וְעָבָ֑דְתָּ וְיַ֤יִן לֹֽא־תִשְׁתֶּה֙ וְלֹ֣א תֶאֱגֹ֔ר כִּ֥י תֹאכְלֶ֖נּוּ הַתֹּלָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Vineyards you will plant and work, and wine not you will drink and not you will gather, for will eat it the worm.
pieces: You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.

L.39: Vineyards you will plant and work, but wine you will not drink, and you will not gather [the grapes], for the worm will eat them.

R.39: You will plant vineyards and work hard in them, but you will not drink any wine or even pick the grapes, because worms will eat them.

decisions.choice: gather: harvest the grapes
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather in and store. Here it is the grapes, and perhaps the wine made from them, that will never be gathered.

decisions.choice: the worm: a pest of vines
decisions.reason: Grubs or caterpillars that eat the buds and the fruit of the vine (Jonah 4:7).

decisions.choice: [the grapes], them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "it", the crop of the vineyard. English names the grapes.

records.source: זֵיתִ֛ים יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּכָל־גְּבוּלֶ֑ךָ וְשֶׁ֨מֶן֙ לֹ֣א תָס֔וּךְ כִּ֥י יִשַּׁ֖ל זֵיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Olive trees will be to you in all your territory, and oil not you will anoint, for will drop off your olive.
pieces: You will have olive trees throughout your country but no oil to rub on your body, because your olives will drop off.

L.40: Olive trees you will have in all your territory, but with oil you will not anoint yourself, for your olives will drop off.

R.40: You will have olive trees all over your land, but you will have no olive oil to put on your skin, because the olives will fall off before they are ripe.

decisions.choice: anoint with oil: rub oil on the skin
decisions.reason: In a hot, dry land people rubbed olive oil into skin and hair to soothe and protect them, especially on days of joy (Ruth 3:3; 2 Samuel 14:2).

decisions.choice: drop off: fall before ripening
decisions.reason: The olives will drop from the trees before they can be pressed for oil.

decisions.choice: before they are ripe
decisions.reason: Readable says why the fallen olives give no oil.

records.source: בָּנִ֥ים וּבָנ֖וֹת תּוֹלִ֑יד וְלֹא־יִהְי֣וּ לָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י יֵלְכ֖וּ בַּשֶּֽׁבִי׃
records.gloss: Sons and daughters you will father, and not they will be to you, for they will go into captivity.
pieces: You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you, because they will be taken away as captives.

L.41: Sons and daughters you will father, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.

R.41: You will have sons and daughters, but you will lose them, because they will be taken away as prisoners of war.

decisions.choice: captivity: carried off by an enemy
decisions.reason: The word is used for people taken away in war to live as captives in a foreign land (21:10; Numbers 21:1).

decisions.choice: have
decisions.reason: The verb is "beget, father", spoken to the people as a whole. Balanced and Readable say "have", which covers both parents; Literal keeps "father".

records.source: כָּל־עֵצְךָ֖ וּפְרִ֣י אַדְמָתֶ֑ךָ יְיָרֵ֖שׁ הַצְּלָצַֽל׃
records.gloss: All your trees and [the] fruit of your ground will take possession of the whirring locust.
pieces: Swarms of insects will take over all your trees and the crops of your land.

L.42: All your trees and the fruit of your ground the whirring locust will take possession of.

R.42: Swarms of insects will eat up all your trees and your crops.

decisions.choice: the whirring locust: a swarming insect
decisions.reason: The word imitates a buzzing or whirring sound and names an insect, probably a kind of locust or cricket. Which one is not certain.

decisions.choice: take possession of: the word used for Israel taking the land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used again and again for Israel taking possession of Canaan (verses 21, 63). Now insects will take possession of what Israel grows.

decisions.choice: swarms of insects
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a general phrase, since the exact insect is not known; Literal says "whirring locust". Readable says "eat up" for "take possession of".

records.source: הַגֵּר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּךָ֔ יַעֲלֶ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ מַ֣עְלָה מָּ֑עְלָה וְאַתָּ֥ה תֵרֵ֖ד מַ֥טָּה מָּֽטָּה׃
records.gloss: The sojourner who [is] in your midst will go up above you upward upward, and you will go down downward downward.
pieces: The outsider living among you will rise above you higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower.

L.43: The sojourner who [is] in your midst will rise above you higher and higher, and you will go down lower and lower.

R.43: The outsiders who live among you will become more and more powerful than you, while you become weaker and weaker.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: an outsider living in Israel without land
decisions.reason: The sojourner was usually poor and needed protection (10:18-19; 24:17). In the curse he becomes greater than the Israelite who owns the land.

decisions.choice: upward upward, downward downward: more and more
decisions.reason: Each word is doubled to show steady increase: the outsider keeps rising and Israel keeps sinking.

decisions.choice: outsider (Balanced); outsiders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourner"; Balanced says "outsider" and Readable "outsiders who live among you", as elsewhere in Deuteronomy.

records.source: ה֣וּא יַלְוְךָ֔ וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹ֣א תַלְוֶ֑נּוּ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְרֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְזָנָֽב׃
records.gloss: He will lend to you, and you not will lend to him; he will become [the] head, and you will become [the] tail.
pieces: He will lend to you, but you will have nothing to lend to him. He will be the head, and you the tail.

L.44: He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him; he will be the head, and you will be the tail.

R.44: They will lend money to you, but you will not have enough to lend to them. They will be the leaders, and you will be the followers.

decisions.choice: lend and borrow, head and tail: verses 12-13 turned around
decisions.reason: The blessings promised Israel would lend and be the head. Now the outsider of verse 43 holds that place.

decisions.choice: They; the leaders, the followers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural for the sojourner of verse 43 and explains "head" and "tail" as in verse 13.

records.source: וּבָ֨אוּ עָלֶ֜יךָ כָּל־הַקְּלָל֣וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּרְדָפ֨וּךָ֙ וְהִשִּׂיג֔וּךָ עַ֖ד הִשָּֽׁמְדָ֑ךְ כִּי־לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֛ר מִצְוֺתָ֥יו וְחֻקֹּתָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And will come on you all the curses these, and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because not you listened to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you.
pieces: All these curses will come on you. They will hunt you down and catch up with you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God by keeping the commandments and statutes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you.

L.45: And all these curses will come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you.

R.45: All these curses will come to you. They will chase you and find you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep the commands and laws {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave you.

decisions.choice: because you did not listen: looking back from the time of the curses
decisions.reason: Moses speaks as if the disobedience has already happened, looking back from the time when the curses have come. The verse rounds off the curses of verses 15-44 with the words of verse 15.

decisions.choice: pursue and overtake
decisions.reason: The curses chase Israel and catch it, as in verses 2, 15 and 22.

decisions.choice: commandments and statutes (Balanced); commands and laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the settled words for this pair in Deuteronomy, as in verse 15.

records.source: וְהָי֣וּ בְךָ֔ לְא֖וֹת וּלְמוֹפֵ֑ת וּֽבְזַרְעֲךָ֖ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will be on you as a sign and as a wonder, and on your offspring, forever.
pieces: They will be a sign and a warning against you and your descendants forever.

L.46: And they will be on you as a sign and as a wonder, and on your offspring, forever.

R.46: These curses will be a sign and a warning to you and your descendants for all time.

decisions.choice: a sign and a wonder: events that show the LORD at work
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Deuteronomy "signs and wonders" are the plagues the LORD sent on Egypt (4:34; 6:22; 7:19). Now Israel itself will become such a sign, showing his judgment to everyone who sees it.

decisions.choice: forever: for generations to come
decisions.reason: The phrase means for a very long time, passing from parents to their descendants.

decisions.choice: a warning
decisions.reason: Here the wonder is a fearful one that teaches a lesson. Balanced and Readable say "warning" so the reader does not hear "wonder" as something good; Literal keeps "wonder".

records.source: תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־עָבַ֨דְתָּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְט֣וּב לֵבָ֑ב מֵרֹ֖ב כֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: Because that not you served Yahweh your God with joy and with goodness of heart from [the] abundance of everything,
pieces: Since you did not serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God joyfully and with a glad heart when you had plenty of everything,

L.47: Because you did not serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with joy and with gladness of heart, from the abundance of everything,

R.47: You had plenty of everything, but you did not serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with joy and a glad heart.

decisions.choice: from the abundance of everything: when you had plenty
alternatives: more than for all your plenty
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean "in the time when you had plenty of everything". They may also mean "because of all your plenty", or that Israel should have served with more joy than all its wealth brought it.

decisions.choice: serve with joy and a glad heart
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy calls Israel to rejoice before the LORD for all he has given (12:7, 12; 16:11; 26:11). Failing to serve him gladly in good times is the reason given for the slavery of verse 48.

decisions.choice: You had plenty of everything, but
decisions.reason: Readable puts the time of plenty first and closes the sentence; verse 48 then begins "So".

records.source: וְעָבַדְתָּ֣ אֶת־אֹיְבֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְשַׁלְּחֶ֤נּוּ יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ בְּרָעָ֧ב וּבְצָמָ֛א וּבְעֵירֹ֖ם וּבְחֹ֣סֶר כֹּ֑ל וְנָתַ֞ן עֹ֤ל בַּרְזֶל֙ עַל־צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ עַ֥ד הִשְׁמִיד֖וֹ אֹתָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: and you will serve your enemies whom will send him Yahweh against you, in hunger and in thirst and in nakedness and in lack of everything; and he will put a yoke of iron on your neck until he has destroyed you.
pieces: you will serve the enemies {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and in need of everything. He will lay an iron yoke on your neck until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has destroyed you.

L.48: and you will serve your enemies whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send against you, in hunger and in thirst and in nakedness and in lack of everything; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will put a yoke of iron on your neck until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has destroyed you.

R.48: So you will serve your enemies, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send against you. You will be hungry, thirsty, without clothes and in need of everything. He will put a heavy iron yoke on your neck, as on an ox, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has destroyed you.

decisions.choice: he will put a yoke ... until he has destroyed you: the LORD
alternatives: the enemy puts the yoke on your neck
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is the LORD, and in Jeremiah 28:14 the LORD says, "I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations." But the enemy has just been spoken of as "him", so the enemy could be the one who puts on the yoke. This translation takes the LORD as the subject.

decisions.choice: a yoke of iron: harsh, unbreakable servitude
decisions.reason: The yoke was the wooden bar laid on the neck of oxen for work. An iron yoke is one that cannot be broken off (Jeremiah 28:13-14; 1 Kings 12:4).

decisions.choice: you will serve: the same word as in verse 47
decisions.reason: Those who would not serve the LORD gladly in plenty will serve their enemies in want.

decisions.choice: heavy; as on an ox
decisions.reason: Readable explains the yoke picture.

records.gloss: Will raise Yahweh against you a nation from afar, from [the] end of the earth, as swoops the eagle, a nation whose language not you will understand,
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle, a nation whose language you will not understand,

L.49: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will raise against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, as the eagle swoops down, a nation whose language you will not understand,

R.49: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring a nation from far away to attack you. It will come from the end of the earth and swoop down on you like an eagle. You will not understand its language.

decisions.choice: eagle: a great bird of prey
decisions.reason: The word can name the eagle or the griffon vulture. The picture is of a sudden, swift attack from far off (Jeremiah 48:40; Habakkuk 1:8).

decisions.choice: from the end of the earth: from very far away
decisions.reason: The phrase points to a distant land beyond Israel's knowledge, as in verse 64.

decisions.choice: a language you will not understand: a wholly foreign enemy
decisions.reason: With no common language there can be no pleading or bargaining (Isaiah 28:11; Jeremiah 5:15).

decisions.choice: three sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long description, which in the Hebrew runs on to verse 51, into short sentences.

records.gloss: a nation fierce of face, which not will lift face to [the] old, and [the] young not will show favor,
pieces: a hard-faced nation that will show no respect to the old and no pity to the young,

L.50: a nation fierce of face, which will not lift up [the] face to the old, and to the young will not show favor,

R.50: Its people will be fierce and cruel. They will show no respect for old people and no pity for children.

decisions.choice: fierce of face: hard and merciless
decisions.reason: A hard face is one that shows no softness or shame (Daniel 8:23; Proverbs 7:13).

decisions.choice: lift up the face to the old: show them regard
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to treat them with favor and respect. Old age was to be honored (Leviticus 19:32), but this nation will spare neither old nor young.

decisions.choice: show no respect, no pity
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idioms mean; Literal keeps "lift up the face" and "show favor".

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and oil, young of cattle and flock: the blessings of 7:13 taken away
decisions.reason: The list is the one the LORD promised to bless in 7:13 and in verse 4. Now a foreign nation will eat it all.

decisions.choice: young of your livestock, harvest of your soil; calves, lambs
decisions.reason: The wording follows verse 4 at each level.

decisions.choice: They
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of the nation as "they", as in verse 50.

records.gloss: And it will besiege you in all your gates until come down your walls the high and the fortified in which you [are] trusting, in all your land; and it will besiege you in all your gates in all your land which has given Yahweh your God to you.
pieces: It will besiege all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trust in come down throughout your land. It will besiege all your towns throughout the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.

L.52: And it will besiege you in all your gates until your high and fortified walls come down, in which you are trusting, in all your land; and it will besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given to you.

R.52: They will surround all your towns and attack them, until the high, strong walls you trust in fall down all over your land. They will attack every town in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.

decisions.choice: your gates: your towns
decisions.reason: The gate stands for the whole walled town, as often in Deuteronomy (12:15; 16:5).

decisions.choice: the walls you trust in
decisions.reason: Israel's high walls will not save it; its safety was in the LORD (1:28-30; 9:1-3).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towns" for "gates"; Literal keeps "gates".

records.gloss: And you will eat [the] fruit of your womb, [the] flesh of your sons and your daughters whom has given to you Yahweh your God, in [the] siege and in [the] distress with which will distress you your enemy.
pieces: Then in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings upon you, you will eat your own children, the flesh of the sons and daughters {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.

L.53: And you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given to you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you.

R.53: When your enemy has you under siege and you are desperate, you will eat your own children, the sons and daughters {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you.

decisions.choice: eating your own children: the horror of a long siege
decisions.reason: When a city was shut in until its food ran out, people starved, and this did happen (2 Kings 6:26-29; Lamentations 2:20; 4:10). Leviticus 26:29 gives the same warning.

decisions.choice: the fruit of your womb: your own children
decisions.reason: The children promised as a blessing in verse 4 become the food of their parents.

decisions.choice: the siege and the distress with which your enemy will distress you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words for "siege" and "distress" sound alike, and "distress" is repeated as a verb. The phrase comes back in verses 55 and 57.

decisions.choice: the siege clause first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the siege first, so the reader knows the setting before the horror that follows. The siege line is worded the same way in verses 55 and 57.

records.source: הָאִישׁ֙ הָרַ֣ךְ בְּךָ֔ וְהֶעָנֹ֖ג מְאֹ֑ד תֵּרַ֨ע עֵינ֤וֹ בְאָחִיו֙ וּבְאֵ֣שֶׁת חֵיק֔וֹ וּבְיֶ֥תֶר בָּנָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹתִֽיר׃
records.gloss: The man the tender among you and the delicate very, will be evil his eye toward his brother and toward [the] wife of his bosom and toward [the] rest of his children whom he has left,
pieces: Even the most gentle and refined man among you will begrudge food to his own brother, to the wife he holds close and to the children he still has left,

L.54: The man who is tender among you and very delicate, his eye will be evil toward his brother and toward the wife of his bosom and toward the rest of his children whom he has left,

R.54: Even the kindest and gentlest man among you will turn cruel and selfish toward his own brother, the wife he loves and the children he still has.

decisions.choice: his eye will be evil: he will begrudge, be mean
decisions.reason: An "evil eye" in Hebrew is a grudging, stingy look, the opposite of generosity (15:9; Proverbs 23:6; 28:22). The man will refuse to share.

decisions.choice: the wife of his bosom: his dearly loved wife
decisions.reason: The wife who lies in his embrace (13:7; Micah 7:5).

decisions.choice: tender and very delicate: used to comfort and refinement
decisions.reason: The words describe a man raised softly, gentle and sensitive. Even such a man will be made heartless by hunger.

decisions.choice: begrudge food (Balanced); turn cruel and selfish (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means; Literal keeps "his eye will be evil". Verse 56 uses the same wording for the woman.
