L.55: so as not to give to any one of them some of the flesh of his children whom he eats, because nothing has been left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in all your gates.

R.55: He will not give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he will have nothing else left when your enemy has you under siege in all your towns and you are desperate.

decisions.choice: from giving: so that he will not give
decisions.reason: The begrudging of verse 54 is explained: he will not share any of the flesh of the children he is eating with the family who are still alive.

decisions.choice: because nothing has been left to him
decisions.reason: He has nothing else to eat, so he keeps even this to himself.

decisions.choice: the siege line as in verse 53; towns
decisions.reason: The siege line is worded as in verse 53, with "in all your gates" (Balanced and Readable "towns", as in verse 52).

records.source: הָרַכָּ֨ה בְךָ֜ וְהָעֲנֻגָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־נִסְּתָ֤ה כַף־רַגְלָהּ֙ הַצֵּ֣ג עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵהִתְעַנֵּ֖ג וּמֵרֹ֑ךְ תֵּרַ֤ע עֵינָהּ֙ בְּאִ֣ישׁ חֵיקָ֔הּ וּבִבְנָ֖הּ וּבְבִתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: The tender and the delicate [woman] among you, who not has tried [the] sole of her foot to set on the ground from delicacy and from tenderness, will be evil her eye toward [the] husband of her bosom and toward her son and toward her daughter,
pieces: The most gentle and refined woman among you, so delicate and pampered that she would never venture to put the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge food to the husband she holds close, to her son and to her daughter,

L.56: The tender and delicate [woman] among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground because of delicacy and tenderness, her eye will be evil toward the husband of her bosom and toward her son and toward her daughter,

R.56: Even the gentlest woman among you, who has lived in such comfort that she would not even set her foot on the ground, will turn cruel and selfish toward the husband she loves and toward her son and daughter.

decisions.choice: would not set the sole of her foot on the ground: so pampered she never walked
decisions.reason: She was so used to comfort that she would not step on the bare ground, being carried or riding wherever she went. The picture shows how far the siege will bring her down.

decisions.choice: her eye will be evil: as in verse 54
decisions.reason: She will begrudge food to her own family, as the man does in verse 54.

decisions.choice: [woman], woman
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adjectives are feminine and need no noun; English supplies "woman" (bracketed at Literal). The rest follows the wording of verse 54.

records.source: וּֽבְשִׁלְיָתָ֞הּ הַיּוֹצֵ֣ת׀מִבֵּ֣ין רַגְלֶ֗יהָ וּבְבָנֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד כִּֽי־תֹאכְלֵ֥ם בְּחֹֽסֶר־כֹּ֖ל בַּסָּ֑תֶר בְּמָצוֹר֙ וּבְמָצ֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצִ֥יק לְךָ֛ אֹיִבְךָ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: and toward her afterbirth which comes out from between her feet and toward her children whom she will bear; for she will eat them in lack of everything in secret, in [the] siege and in [the] distress with which will distress you your enemy in your gates.
pieces: and to the afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and to the children she bears. For she will eat them in secret, having nothing else at all, in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings upon you in your towns.

L.57: and toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and toward her children whom she bears; for she will eat them secretly for lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in your gates.

R.57: She will not share even the afterbirth or the baby she gives birth to. She will eat them secretly, because she will have nothing else to eat when your enemy has you under siege in your towns and you are desperate.

decisions.choice: afterbirth: what comes out after the baby
decisions.reason: The word means the placenta and membranes that come out after birth. "From between her feet" is a modest way of speaking about childbirth.

decisions.choice: she will eat them in secret
decisions.reason: She hides the newborn and the afterbirth so as not to share them. 2 Kings 6:28-29 and Lamentations 4:10 tell of mothers driven to this in a siege.

decisions.choice: her legs
decisions.reason: Balanced says "legs" for "feet", since in English "between her feet" does not suggest childbirth. Literal keeps "feet".

records.source: אִם־לֹ֨א תִשְׁמֹ֜ר לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵי֙ הַתּוֹרָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את הַכְּתוּבִ֖ים בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה לְ֠יִרְאָה אֶת־הַשֵּׁ֞ם הַנִּכְבָּ֤ד וְהַנּוֹרָא֙ הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: If not you take care to do all [the] words of the law this which [are] written in the book this, to fear the name the glorious and the awesome this, Yahweh your God,
pieces: If you do not carefully keep every word of this law written in this book, and do not fear this glorious and awesome name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

L.58: If you do not take care to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

R.58: Be careful to obey every word of the teaching written in this book. Fear the glorious and awesome name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: this law: the whole of Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching, the whole of what Moses sets before Israel, not only its rules (1:5; 4:44).

decisions.choice: written in this book: Moses' teaching set down in writing
decisions.reason: This is the first time in the chapter that the teaching is spoken of as a written book. Moses later writes it down and gives it to the priests (17:18; 31:9, 24-26).

decisions.choice: this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God
decisions.reason: The name stands for the LORD himself as he has made himself known. "The LORD your God" stands after it and says whose name it is.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for this word, as elsewhere in Deuteronomy; Literal and Balanced say "law".

decisions.choice: two commands; the condition in verse 59
decisions.reason: Readable states what Israel must do as commands and gives "If you do not" at the start of verse 59. Literal and Balanced keep the condition open into verse 59.

records.source: וְהִפְלָ֤א יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מַכֹּ֣תְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת מַכּ֣וֹת זַרְעֶ֑ךָ מַכּ֤וֹת גְּדֹלוֹת֙ וְנֶ֣אֱמָנ֔וֹת וָחֳלָיִ֥ם רָעִ֖ים וְנֶאֱמָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: and will make extraordinary Yahweh your plagues and [the] plagues of your offspring, plagues great and lasting, and sicknesses severe and lasting.
pieces: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike you and your descendants with astonishing plagues, great and lasting plagues and severe and lasting sicknesses.

L.59: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make your plagues extraordinary, and the plagues of your offspring, great and lasting plagues, and severe and lasting sicknesses.

R.59: If you do not, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send terrible plagues on you and your descendants. They will be great disasters that do not end and severe sicknesses that do not go away.

decisions.choice: make extraordinary: beyond anything ordinary
decisions.reason: The verb is from the same root as the "wonders" the LORD did in Egypt. Here the plagues on Israel will be wonders of judgment, beyond what is normal.

decisions.choice: lasting: long and unrelenting
decisions.reason: The word means firm or faithful; said of plagues and sicknesses, it means they will hold on and not let go.

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" brings the result of the condition in verse 58, so Literal and Balanced say "then".

records.source: וְהֵשִׁ֣יב בְּךָ֗ אֵ֚ת כָּל־מַדְוֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגֹ֖רְתָּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְדָבְק֖וּ בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And he will bring back on you all [the] diseases of Egypt which you were afraid of them, and they will cling to you.
pieces: He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.

L.60: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring back on you every disease of Egypt that you were afraid of, and they will cling to you.

R.60: He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt that frightened you, and they will not leave you.

decisions.choice: the diseases of Egypt
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised to keep these diseases from an obedient Israel (7:15; Exodus 15:26). Now he will bring them back. Israel, rescued from Egypt, will suffer what Egypt suffered.

pieces: Though you were as many as the stars in the sky, only a few of you will be left, because you did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.62: And you will be left few in number, whereas you were like the stars of the heavens in multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: like the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham descendants as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17), and Moses has said the promise came true (1:10; 10:22). The curse undoes it.

decisions.choice: men of fewness: few people
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 4:27 and 26:5 for a small number of people.

decisions.choice: Though you were (Balanced); There were (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the former great number first, as a contrast, and then the few who are left.

pieces: Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delighted in doing you good and making you many, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will delight in making you perish and destroying you. You will be torn away from the land you are entering to take possession of.

L.63: And it will be: as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rejoice over you to make you perish and to destroy you; and you will be torn away from the land that you are going into to take possession of.

R.63: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was glad to do good things for you and to make you a great nation. In the same way, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be glad to destroy you and wipe you out. You will be pulled up from the land you are going into to take as your own.

decisions.choice: the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you
decisions.reason: The words are meant to shock. The LORD who delighted to bless Israel will carry out its punishment just as fully. The same picture is turned back to good in 30:9: the LORD will again rejoice over Israel for good, as he rejoiced over its ancestors.

decisions.choice: torn away: uprooted
decisions.reason: The verb is used of pulling something up by the roots or tearing it out (Proverbs 2:22; Psalm 52:7). Israel will be pulled out of its land.

decisions.choice: the land phrase as in verse 21
decisions.reason: The words about the land are those of verse 21 at each level.

pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods of wood and stone.

L.64: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among all the peoples, from the end of the earth to the end of the earth, and there you will serve other gods that you have not known, you and your fathers, wood and stone.

R.64: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will scatter you among the nations all over the earth, from one end to the other. There you will worship other gods that you and your ancestors never knew, idols made of wood and stone.

decisions.choice: scatter you among all the peoples
decisions.reason: Moses warned of this scattering in 4:27-28, and Leviticus 26:33 says the same.

decisions.choice: other gods, wood and stone: as in verse 36
decisions.reason: Idols made by human hands.

decisions.choice: as in verse 36
decisions.reason: The wording for the gods follows verse 36 at each level.

records.gloss: And among the nations those not you will find rest, and not will be a resting place for [the] sole of your foot; and will give Yahweh to you there a heart trembling and failing of eyes and despair of soul.
pieces: Among those nations you will find no rest, no place to rest the sole of your foot. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you an anxious heart, eyes worn out with longing and a despairing spirit.

L.65: And among those nations you will find no rest, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you there a trembling heart and failing of eyes and despair of soul.

R.65: Among those nations you will never be at ease, and you will never have a place to settle. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make you always afraid. Your eyes will grow tired from waiting for help, and you will lose all hope.

decisions.choice: no resting place for the sole of your foot: nowhere to settle
decisions.reason: The words recall the dove that found no place to rest its foot and came back to the ark (Genesis 8:9).

decisions.choice: failing of eyes: as in verse 32
decisions.reason: Eyes worn out with looking for help that never comes.

decisions.choice: despair of soul: the inner life fading away
decisions.reason: The word for "soul" is the whole living self. Its "despair" is a pining or fainting away, the loss of all hope.

decisions.choice: always afraid
decisions.reason: Readable says what a trembling heart means.

records.source: וְהָי֣וּ חַיֶּ֔יךָ תְּלֻאִ֥ים לְךָ֖ מִנֶּ֑גֶד וּפָֽחַדְתָּ֙ לַ֣יְלָה וְיוֹמָ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַאֲמִ֖ין בְּחַיֶּֽיךָ׃

pieces: Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will live in dread night and day, never sure that you will survive.

L.66: And your life will be hanging [in doubt] before you, and you will be in dread night and day, and you will not be sure of your life.

R.66: Your life will always be in danger. You will be terrified night and day, never knowing whether you will live.

decisions.choice: your life will be hanging before you: in constant danger
decisions.reason: Life hangs as if by a thread, with no assurance that it will last.

decisions.choice: not be sure of your life: have no confidence that you will live
decisions.reason: The verb means to trust or be firm; here, to feel no certainty that one will stay alive (Job 24:22).

decisions.choice: [in doubt]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words English needs to make sense of "hanging".

records.gloss: In the morning you will say, Who will give evening? and in the evening you will say, Who will give morning? from [the] dread of your heart which you will dread and from [the] sight of your eyes which you will see.
pieces: In the morning you will say, 'If only evening would come!' and in the evening, 'If only morning would come!' because of the dread that fills your heart and the sights your eyes will see.

L.67: In the morning you will say, 'Who will give [it to be] evening!' and in the evening you will say, 'Who will give [it to be] morning!' because of the dread of your heart that you will dread and because of the sight of your eyes that you will see.

R.67: When morning comes you will say, 'I wish it were evening!' And when evening comes you will say, 'I wish it were morning!' You will feel this way because of the terror in your heart and the terrible things you will see.

decisions.choice: Who will give ...: If only ...
decisions.reason: "Who will give" is a Hebrew way of saying "if only" (5:29). Each part of the day is so dreadful that people long for the next.

decisions.choice: because of the dread ... and the sight
decisions.reason: The reason is given twice: the fear inside them and what they see around them (verse 34).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: These words are quoted inside Moses' speech, so they take single quotation marks.

records.gloss: And will bring you back Yahweh [to] Egypt in ships, by the way which I said to you, Not you will again see it, and you will sell yourselves there to your enemies as male slaves and as female slaves, and there [will be] no buyer.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way I promised you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as slaves, men and women, but there will be no buyer."

L.68: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way about which I said to you, 'You will never see it again'; and there you will sell yourselves to your enemies as male slaves and as female slaves, but [there will be] no one buying."

R.68: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send you back to Egypt in ships, on the journey I told you that you would never make again. There you will try to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, but no one will want to buy you."

decisions.choice: back to Egypt by the way you will never see again: the exodus undone
decisions.reason: The LORD had said that Israel must never go back to Egypt (17:16; Exodus 14:13). The last curse is a return to the land of slavery, as if the rescue from Egypt had never happened.

decisions.choice: I said to you: Moses passing on the LORD's word
decisions.reason: In 17:16 it is the LORD who said "You shall never again return that way". Here Moses says "I said", either because he gave that word to Israel or because, as in verse 20, the LORD's own voice speaks through him.

decisions.choice: in ships; you will sell yourselves, but no one will buy
decisions.reason: Ships may point to captives carried off and sold by traders over the sea (Ezekiel 27:13; Joel 4:6). The verb means to offer oneself for sale. Israel will be worth so little that no one will want them even as slaves.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: People are offered for sale as property here, so "slaves" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Moses' words, which opened at 27:12, end with this verse, so the double quotation mark closes here.

records.gloss: These [are the] words of the covenant which commanded Yahweh Moses to make with [the] sons of Israel in [the] land of Moab, besides the covenant which he made with them at Horeb.
pieces: These are the words of the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses to make in the land of Moab with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, besides the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with them at Horeb.

L.69: These [are] the words of the covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses to make with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with them at Horeb.

R.69: These are the terms of the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses to make with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in the land of Moab. This covenant was in addition to the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with them at Mount Horeb.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 28:69 is 29:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does, where chapter 28 has 69 verses. Many Bibles begin chapter 29 with this verse, so 28:69 here is 29:1 there, and 29:1-28 here is 29:2-29 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: These are the words: a heading that looks back or forward
decisions.reason: The verse may close the covenant teaching of chapters 5-28, as the Hebrew chapter division takes it, or introduce the speech that begins in 29:1, as the other numbering takes it. Similar lines both close (Leviticus 26:46) and open (1:1) sections. Either way it names what Moses has taught in Moab as covenant words.

decisions.choice: the covenant made at Horeb
decisions.reason: The covenant of Sinai, also called Horeb, made forty years earlier (5:2-3). The covenant in Moab renews it with the new generation about to enter the land.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks here, after Moses' words closed at the end of verse 68.
